subject: Proposed short rollback & SLA carveout for SunWave — model v7z p95 instability
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-22T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: spike in p95 for model v7z — impact on SunWave

Vanessa / Laura,

We started seeing a region-wide shift in tail latency for model v7z at 07:40 PT. p95 for SunWave traffic has moved from ~520ms to intermittent 1.1–1.3s over the last 30m; p99 also has a few outliers up to ~2.2s. Canary traffic confirms the regression reproduces on the v7z variant (v7z_20280621).

Quick notes: 
- Affected infra: hosted-us-west and dedicated-us-west pools serving SunWave (pinned routing).
- Triggered by a kernel selection change rolled 2028-06-21 23:50 PT (auto-optimizer).
- No error-rate increase; this is latency-only but violates client p95 SLA target.

Attached a short plot (p95_drift_plot.png) with rolling windows by minute. My read: safest mitigation is to roll traffic back to the last-known-stable model binary (v7y_20280620) and perform the optimizer change in a canary environment for longer telemetry.

Operational ask: approval to perform a targeted rollback for SunWave (and optionally other pinned accounts) with a 30–60 minute maintenance window. Also recommend a temporary SLA carveout for the window (we should communicate proactively).

I can run the rollback; need authorization from ops (Laura) for the change window and a sales-approved client message (Vanessa).

Ben

Attachment: p95_drift_plot.png (image/png)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: spike in p95 for model v7z — impact on SunWave

Thanks Ben — useful triage.

Objective: minimize customer impact and keep the account healthy. I will draft the customer-facing message but need two confirmations before I send:
1) Laura — ops signoff on rollback plan + expected duration and risk profile. Can we contain this to a 30–45 minute window with safe fallback?
2) Ben — confirm rollback will not change embedding versions or require schema changes for SunWave. They cannot tolerate any embedding drift.

If both answers are yes, I want to request a 45-minute maintenance window starting as early as 10:30 PT. I’ll offer SunWave a one-hour credit for the incident if they agree.

I drafted a short customer note below — will send after your replies unless you suggest edits.

—Vanessa

> Vanessa / Laura,
> 
> We started seeing a region-wide shift in tail latency for model v7z at 07:40 PT. p95 for SunWave traffic has moved from ~520ms to intermittent 1.1–1.3s over the last 30m; p99 also has a few outliers up to ~2.2s....

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-22T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: spike in p95 for model v7z — impact on SunWave

Agree with Ben. Ops is green on a targeted rollback to v7y_20280620 for SunWave only; plan and caveats below.

Rollback plan (summary):
- Pre-change: freeze configuration for the account, snapshot current routing and KV cache. Notify monitoring and on-call (infra) 15m prior.
- Change: demote v7z variant for the SunWave route and repoint to v7y_20280620 (can be done on the routing layer).
- Validation: run 5m synthetic traffic + customer traffic watch for 20m; if p95 returns to baseline, keep change. If not, rollback to v7z and open escalation.
- Post-change: collect logs and short incident note.

Risk profile: low to moderate. There is no model format change — only kernel selection and a model binary variant swap. Embeddings are unchanged for this account. Expected customer impact: brief 1–2 minute routing convergence possible, otherwise improvement.

I recommend: 45-minute window starting 10:30 PT. I will be on-call and Ben will execute the routing change. I’ve uploaded the rollback steps: rollback_plan_v7y_20280620.md and added the runbook link below.

Laura

Attachment: rollback_plan_v7y_20280620.md (text/markdown)

Related: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-rollback-v7z
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Holt <alex.holt@sunwave.com>
Cc: procurement@sunwave.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-22T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Planned short rollback for SunWave traffic — request to proceed (10:30 PT target)

Alex — brief heads-up from Redwood on a short operational mitigation we propose to resolve a burst of increased latency for your traffic served by model v7z.

What we saw: starting ~07:40 PT today our telemetry showed a p95 increase for your traffic (from ~520ms to intermittent 1.1–1.3s). This is a latency regression tied to a recent optimizer change applied to the v7z variant. No increase in error rates or incorrect outputs was observed.

What we propose: a targeted rollback of routing for SunWave back to the previously stable variant (v7y_20280620). Plan is to execute a controlled change during a short maintenance window this morning: 10:30–11:15 PT (45 minutes). Expected impact: brief (~1–2m) request re-routing while the change converges; then p95 should return to baseline.

Why this helps: the optimizer change changed kernel selection under specific sequence-length patterns and produced higher tail latency in our canary and production slices. Rolling back the variant removes that change while we re-run the optimizer in a gated canary.

Compensation and SLA: we propose a 1-hour service credit for the window if you experience any degradation during the operation. We also request your permission to mark this action as a short SLA exception for today’s targeted mitigation (we will document it in the incident log).

Request: please reply with APPROVE to proceed or let us know if you need a different time. If we don’t hear back by 10:10 PT we will hold and keep you updated.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0117
